mainTopic: The end of פרק כיסוי הדם, the opening משנה of פרק גיד הנשה, and the גמרא's analysis of why the משנה says the איסור applies to מוקדשין.
overview: The amud opens by finishing פרק כיסוי הדם. A שופר or לולב of עבודה זרה is invalid because those מצוות need a minimum size, and עבודה זרה is treated as already crushed to powder. Covering blood needs no size, and crushed ash covers even better, so ash of עבודה זרה may be used. After the הדרן, פרק גיד הנשה begins with a משנה: the איסור of גיד הנשה applies everywhere and at all times, to חולין and קדשים, to בהמה and חיה, and to both legs, but not to birds. The משנה also records a מחלוקת about a שליל, and a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים about trusting butchers. The גמרא then asks why the משנה needs to mention מוקדשין at all. It tries a few explanations and finally says the case is the unborn offspring of a קרבן, where the גיד prohibition and the holiness prohibition arrive at the same moment, so both take hold. The גמרא defends this reading against a question from the wording of the משנה. It then begins a new challenge from a משנה about a נזיר and רבי יוחנן's explanation about a נפל whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why idol-worship ash still works for covering blood
steps.stepSummary: A שופר or לולב needs a minimum size, and עבודה זרה is treated as crushed, so it fails. Covering blood has no minimum size, and crushed ash is even better.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a שופר and a לולב we need a minimum size, and an object of עבודה זרה is treated as if it were already crushed, so it has no size. Here, for covering blood, the more crushed the ash is, the better it is for covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question: why a שופר or לולב of עבודה זרה is invalid, while ash of עבודה זרה may be used for כיסוי הדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה must be burned and destroyed, so הלכה treats it as if it has already been ground to dust. That ruins anything that needs a minimum size, like a שופר or לולב. כיסוי הדם needs no size at all, and fine dust covers best, so being 'crushed' does not hurt it.

keyTerms.meaning: A minimum required size or measure.
Idol worship; here, an object used for idol worship.
Its size is considered crushed. Since it must be destroyed, הלכה treats it as already ground to powder.
Covering, meaning the מצוה of covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or חיה.

steps.whatToRemember: כתותי מכתת שיעורא only disqualifies a מצוה that needs a minimum size. כיסוי הדם has no minimum size, so ash of עבודה זרה still works.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean עבודה זרה becomes permitted. It means the 'crushed' status causes no problem for a מצוה that has no size requirement.

phrases.english: we require a minimum measure,
phrases.notes: He means there, by a שופר and a לולב, which must be a certain size.

phrases.english: and an object of idol worship,
its size is considered crushed.
phrases.notes: Since it must be burned, הלכה treats it as if it were already powder, so it has no size.

phrases.english: Here, the more it is crushed,
the better it is for covering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised just before this section: how ash of עבודה זרה differs from a שופר or לולב of עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases: a מצוה that needs a minimum size versus one that does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that whatever is invalid for one מצוה because it is עבודה זרה should be invalid for כיסוי הדם too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The problem with עבודה זרה is that its size is treated as crushed. That only matters where a minimum size is needed, which is not the case for כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כיסוי הדם
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marking the end of פרק כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק כיסוי הדם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the end of the פרק about covering blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the standard farewell line said when a פרק is finished. It is not a legal statement; it shows that a new topic is about to start.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the traditional words said when finishing a פרק.
Covering the blood; the name of the פרק now ending.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Covering the Blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק that the previous step finished.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק כיסוי הדם is complete; a new perek begins.

steps.title: Where and to what the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that גיד הנשה applies in ארץ ישראל and outside it, with or without the בית המקדש, to חולין and קדשים, to בהמה and חיה, and to both legs. It does not apply to birds, because they have no כף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prohibition of גיד הנשה applies in ארץ ישראל and outside ארץ ישראל, while the בית המקדש stands and when it does not, to חולין and to קדשים. It applies to a בהמה and to a חיה, to the right thigh and to the left thigh. It does not apply to a bird, because a bird has no 'spoon' of the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens. The משנה lists all the situations where the איסור of גיד הנשה applies and one where it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list shows that this איסור does not depend on place, on time, or on the holiness of the animal. The one exclusion, birds, comes from the פסוק's words 'על כף הירך': a bird's thigh lacks the rounded, spoon-shaped part, so the איסור does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve in the thigh, which is forbidden to eat.
While the בית המקדש is standing.
Ordinary animals, and animals set aside as קרבנות.
Domesticated animals (like cows) and wild animals (like deer).
The 'spoon' of the thigh, the rounded part of the hip where the גיד lies.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the full scope of a practical איסור that applies today in every kosher kitchen. The rest of the פרק explores its details.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The sciatic nerve applies
phrases.notes: He means the איסור of eating it applies.

phrases.english: in the Land of Israel and outside the Land,
in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple,
to non-sacred animals and to sacrificial animals,
and it applies to domesticated and to wild animals,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָרֵךְ שֶׁל יָמִין וּבְיָרֵךְ שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל,
phrases.english: to the right thigh and to the left thigh,
but it does not apply to a bird,
because it has no 'spoon'.
phrases.notes: This refers to 'כף הירך' in the פסוק, בראשית 32:33.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ גיד הנשה נוהג בארץ ובחוצה לארץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק and a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גיד הנשה is forbidden in all places and times, in חולין and קדשים, in בהמה and חיה, and in both legs, but not in birds, which lack a כף הירך.

steps.title: Does the prohibition apply to an unborn calf?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says גיד הנשה applies to a שליל. רבי יהודה says it does not, and that the שליל's חלב is permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The איסור applies to a fetus. רבי יהודה says it does not apply to a fetus, and its fat is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case, a שליל, and records a disagreement about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, a שליל counts as an animal for גיד הנשה. רבי יהודה disagrees and goes further: he also permits the שליל's חלב. So in his view a שליל is not subject to these איסורים.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus, an unborn animal found inside its slaughtered mother.
Certain forbidden fats of a בהמה.
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה.

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת about a שליל: the תנא קמא forbids its גיד הנשה, while רבי יהודה permits both its גיד and its חלב.

phrases.english: And it applies to a fetus.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It does not apply to a fetus,
and its fat is permitted.
phrases.notes: 'Its fat' means the forbidden-type fat of the fetus.

steps.triggerLanguage: ונוהג בשליל רבי יהודה אומר אינו נוהג בשליל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with a disputed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: גיד הנשה applies to a שליל. רבי יהודה: it does not, and the שליל's חלב is permitted.

steps.title: Can butchers be trusted to remove the sciatic nerve?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says butchers are not trusted about the גיד הנשה. חכמים say they are trusted about it and also about חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Butchers are not trusted about the sciatic nerve, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say they are trusted about it and about the forbidden fat.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It asks whether we can rely on a butcher's word that he removed the forbidden parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not rely on butchers to remove the גיד הנשה. The חכמים trust them both for the גיד הנשה and for חלב, the forbidden fat.

keyTerms.meaning: Butchers
Trusted; we can rely on their word
Forbidden fat of an animal

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is now complete. Next, the גמרא starts analyzing its earlier lines, beginning with the word מוקדשין.

phrases.english: And butchers are not trusted
regarding the sciatic nerve,
phrases.notes: He means trusting the butcher's word that he removed it.

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the Sages say:
They are trusted about it and about the forbidden fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין הַטַּבָּחִין נֶאֱמָנִין עַל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה that opened in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: butchers are not trusted on גיד הנשה. חכמים: they are trusted on it and on חלב.

steps.title: Why say it applies to sacrifices? Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that גיד הנשה applies to מוקדשין. Surely making an animal holy does not cancel the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Sacrificial animals? That's obvious! Just because he made it holy, does the sciatic nerve prohibition fall away from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges the word מוקדשין in the משנה (from step 3). It argues that this rule seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one would think that making an animal holy erases a Torah prohibition that was already on it. So the משנה must be teaching something new by mentioning מוקדשין. The next steps try to find out what that new point is.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside as קרבנות (sacrifices)
It's obvious; why say it?
Fell away, got cancelled

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Sacrificial animals? That's obvious!
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's line that גיד הנשה applies to sacrificial animals too.

phrases.english: Just because he consecrated it,
does the nerve prohibition fall away from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first גמרא question on the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to mention מוקדשין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making an animal holy cannot cancel a prohibition already on it, so saying the rule applies to sacrifices seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Maybe the holiness prohibition adds on top? Then the wording would be different
steps.stepSummary: One possible answer: a nerve has taste, so the holiness prohibition takes hold on top of the גיד prohibition. The גמרא rejects this, because then the משנה would have said 'מוקדשין applies to the גיד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say nerves have taste, and the prohibition of holy animals comes and takes hold on top of the nerve prohibition, then the משנה should have said: 'the holiness prohibition applies to the nerve.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a possible answer to the 'obvious' question and knocks it down in the same breath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one prohibition cannot take hold where another is already in place (אין איסור חל על איסור). The suggestion is that the משנה's new point is that the holiness prohibition still takes hold on the nerve. But then the משנה's subject should have been the holiness prohibition ('מוקדשין applies to the nerve'). It is not 'the nerve rule applies to מוקדשין', which is how the משנה actually reads.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives off taste, so it counts as real food
A second prohibition usually cannot take hold where one already exists
Takes effect, takes hold
It should have said

steps.confusionAlert: The rejection is about wording. The question is which prohibition is the subject of the sentence. The משנה says 'גיד applies to holy animals', not 'holiness applies to the גיד'.

phrases.english: And if you would say
nerves do have taste,
and the prohibition of holy animals comes
and takes hold on top of the nerve prohibition,
then 'the holiness prohibition applies to the nerve'
is what it should have said.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא יֵשׁ בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 6 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the משנה teaches that the holiness prohibition adds on top of the nerve prohibition
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording makes the גיד prohibition the subject, not the holiness prohibition.

steps.title: Nerves have no taste, so only the nerve prohibition applies
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the תנא holds that nerves have no taste. So in a sacrifice the nerve is forbidden only because of the גיד prohibition, with no extra holiness prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he holds that nerves have no taste. So with holy animals, the nerve prohibition is there, but the holiness prohibition is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of why the משנה mentions מוקדשין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a nerve has no taste, it is not really food. So the prohibition on eating holy meat does not apply to it. The משנה is telling us that in a sacrifice the nerve is still forbidden, but only because of גיד הנשה.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, his opinion is
There is / there is not

phrases.english: Rather, he holds
that nerves have no taste,
and with holy animals, the nerve prohibition is there,
but the holiness prohibition is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קָסָבַר אֵין בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes a specific opinion to the תנא (nerves have no taste)
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that in a sacrifice only the גיד prohibition applies to the nerve, with no holiness prohibition.

steps.title: But another משנה says the nerve does give off taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 8. Another משנה rules that a thigh cooked with its nerve is forbidden if the nerve gave off enough taste, so nerves do have taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does our תנא really hold that nerves have no taste? But we learned: a thigh that was cooked with the sciatic nerve in it, if there is enough to give taste, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by quoting a משנה from later in this פרק. The next step accepts this challenge and drops the 'no taste' answer for a new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 depended on the idea that nerves have no taste. But the later משנה forbids the whole thigh when the nerve's taste spread into it. That only makes sense if a nerve does have taste, so the answer in step 8 seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of our משנה
Thigh (the leg where the nerve sits)
Forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge forces the גמרא to find a completely new explanation for why the משנה mentions מוקדשין.

phrases.english: And does the תנא of our משנה hold
that nerves have no taste?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
a thigh that was cooked with the sciatic nerve in it,
if there is enough in it to give taste,
it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר תַּנָּא דִּידַן אֵין בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our תנא holds nerves have no taste
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה forbids a thigh because of the nerve's taste, which shows nerves do have taste.

steps.title: The case is the unborn offspring of a sacrifice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. The משנה is talking about ולדות קדשים. The תנא holds that גיד הנשה applies to a fetus, and that offspring of sacrifices are holy while still in the womb. So the גיד prohibition and the holiness prohibition arrive at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we are dealing here with the offspring of sacrifices. The תנא holds that the prohibition applies to a fetus. He also holds that offspring of sacrifices are already holy inside their mother's womb. So the גיד prohibition and the holiness prohibition come at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 9 showed that a nerve does have taste, which broke the earlier answer. So the גמרא now offers a completely new answer about which case the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the גיד prohibition is already on the animal, and the holiness of a קרבן comes later. Under אין איסור חל על איסור, the holiness prohibition could not then take hold on the nerve. But this תנא holds that a fetus of a holy animal is already holy in the womb, and that the גיד prohibition applies to a fetus. So both prohibitions arrive at the same moment, and the holiness prohibition also takes hold on the nerve. That is the new point the משנה makes by mentioning מוקדשין.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring of sacrificial animals
A fetus (unborn calf or lamb) found inside its slaughtered mother
Inside their mother's womb
The prohibition that comes from an animal being holy (a sacrifice)
Together, at the same time

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two 'קסבר' points here. The first is that גיד הנשה applies to a fetus at all. The second is that the offspring is already holy in the womb. You need both points for the two prohibitions to arrive together.

phrases.english: Rather, here we are dealing with offspring of sacrifices,
and he holds that it applies to a fetus,
and he holds that offspring of sacrifices
are holy while in their mother's womb,
so that the prohibition of the sinew and the prohibition of holy things
come together at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from step 8, which step 9 knocked down, with a new reading of the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed pointless, since holiness would not cancel the גיד prohibition, and the 'no taste' explanation failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a holy fetus, where both prohibitions arrive at once. So the holiness prohibition takes hold on the nerve together with the גיד prohibition, and both apply.

steps.title: The later clause shows the first clause is not about a fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. The סיפא of the משנה separately says 'it applies to a fetus.' That implies the רישא is not talking about a fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really explain the first clause as being about a fetus? The later clause teaches 'it applies to a fetus.' This shows that the first clause is not dealing with a fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 10 using the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רישא were already about a fetus, there would be no reason for the סיפא to add a new line saying the law applies to a fetus. Saying it separately suggests the fetus is a new case. That would mean the רישא was about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: You set up (explain) the case as
The later clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה
By implication, it follows that

phrases.english: But can you really set it up as a fetus?
Since the later clause teaches 'it applies to a fetus,'
it follows that in the first clause we are not dealing with a fetus!
phrases.notes: The 'it applies to a fetus' line is the רבנן's view; רבי יהודה disagrees there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case setup proposed in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 10 that the רישא is about a fetus
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate ruling about a fetus in the סיפא would be extra if the רישא already dealt with a fetus. So the רישא must be about something else.

steps.title: The later clause points to the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סיפא is not a new case. It explains that the matter in the רישא (the law for a fetus) is a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: this matter is a disagreement between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 10 by re-reading the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא is not adding a new case. It is telling us that the fetus case of the רישא is debated: the רבנן say the law applies to a fetus, and רבי יהודה says it does not. So the רישא can still be about a fetus, following the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא re-reads the text)
A disagreement between sages

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה מַחְלוֹקֶת דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: This matter is a dispute between רבי יהודה and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 and keeps the reading of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא seemed to be a new case, which would mean the רישא was not about a fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא only reports the מחלוקת about the fetus case. It is not a separate case.

steps.title: Do the two prohibitions really arrive together? A משנה about a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the גיד prohibition and the holiness prohibition really come at the same time. It begins to bring proof from a משנה: a נזיר shaves for impurity from a corpse and from an olive-bulk of a corpse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really say that both prohibitions come at the same time? But we learned in a משנה: a נזיר shaves for these kinds of impurity: for a corpse, and for an olive-bulk of a corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second challenge to step 10. It is setting up a proof that will be built over the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the גמרא is not attacking the wording. It is attacking the claim that both prohibitions arrive at the same moment. The משנה in נזיר is the starting point, and the real point of the proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow not to drink wine, not to cut his hair, and not to become impure from the dead
Shaves (a נזיר who became impure shaves and restarts his נזירות)
Kinds of ritual impurity
An olive-sized piece of flesh from a dead body

phrases.english: And can you really say
that both of them come at the same time?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: עַל אֵלּוּ טוּמְאוֹת הַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ,
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: For these impurities the נזיר shaves:

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַמֵּת וְעַל כְּזַיִת מִן הַמֵּת.
phrases.english: for a corpse, and for an olive-bulk of a corpse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי קָאָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second, new challenge against step 10, now about timing rather than wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 10 that the גיד prohibition and the holiness prohibition arrive together

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a miscarried fetus whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in נזיר seems to repeat itself, because a whole corpse is obviously worse than an olive-bulk. רבי יוחנן explains that 'a corpse' teaches about a נפל whose limbs were not yet joined by sinews.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was hard for us: if he shaves for an olive-bulk of a corpse, then all the more so for a whole corpse! And רבי יוחנן said: it was needed only for a miscarried fetus whose limbs were not yet joined by sinews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the background of the נזיר משנה. It brings רבי יוחנן's explanation, which is the key fact the challenge relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'a corpse' looks extra, since an olive-bulk already makes the נזיר shave. רבי יוחנן says it teaches about an early miscarried fetus. It counts as a whole corpse, but it does not have an olive-bulk of flesh, because its limbs are not yet joined by sinews. This shows that a fetus exists at a stage before its sinews have connected its limbs, and the גמרא will use that to question the timing in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so
It was needed only for (this special case)
A miscarried fetus
Its limbs became joined by sinews

phrases.english: And it was difficult for us:
for an olive-bulk of a corpse he shaves,
for the whole of it, all the more so, no?
And רבי יוחנן said:
It was needed only for a miscarried fetus
whose limbs had not been joined by sinews.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'were joined.'
